territorial_scope.description: Statutory instrument made under UK legislation; it amends and brings into force provisions relating to the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, and states no separate geographic extent.

evidence.quote: The Secretary of State makes these Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 142(1) and 143(1)

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Commencement regulations bringing into force specified provisions of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 on 5 February 2026 and 19 June 2026, with transitional and saving rules for data subject requests, automated decision-making, penalty notices, complaints handling and PEC Regulations enforcement. Addressed to controllers and the Information Commissioner.
summary.long: The Regulations (SI 2026/82), made on 29 January 2026 by the Secretary of State, bring into force on 5 February 2026 provisions of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 listed in regulation 2, including provisions on research and statistical purposes, consent for scientific research, lawfulness of processing, purpose limitation, responses to data subjects' requests, automated decision-making, children's higher protection, third-country transfers, and the Information Commissioner's enforcement powers under the PEC Regulations. Section 103 and Schedule 10 (complaints by data subjects) come into force on 19 June 2026. Savings provide that the amended time limits for responding to requests (section 76) do not apply to requests received before 5 February 2026, the automated decision-making amendments (section 80 and Schedule 6) do not apply to decisions taken before that date, and the penalty-notice amendments (section 101) do not apply where a notice of intent was given before that date. Complaint-handling duties apply only to complaints received on or after 19 June 2026. Regulations 8 to 11 set transitional rules for PEC Regulations enforcement, under which pre-commencement breaches are governed by the earlier regime. Regulation 12 updates commencement references in the Data Protection Act 2018.

Internal inconsistencies: reg 8(1) cites 'regulation 319' of the PEC Regulations, while the explanatory note cites 'regulation 31'; reg 7 cites 'section 164A(3) and (4)' of the 2018 Act, while the explanatory note writes '164(A)(3) and (4)'. The 'Note as to earlier Commencement Regulations' (SI 2025/904, 2025/996, 2025/982, 2025/1213, 2026/31) is non-operative and is not recorded as relations. Section 138 of the 2025 Act is marked as not yet in force on the making date, with commencement on 6 February 2026 per that note.

thresholds.note: This commencement regulation sets commencement dates and temporal savings cut-offs (e.g., requests received before 5th February 2026; decisions taken before 5th February 2026). These are recorded as events and savings provisions, not numeric thresholds. The text states no monetary, size, age, volume, eligibility or penalty-tier cut-offs, and no penalty maxima.
